conflicts.name: Russia–Ukraine war
conflicts.status: Slow Donbas grind, record strikes on Ukraine's grid; US-led talks set for Nov 10-11
conflicts.summary: Russia's full-scale invasion, begun in February 2022, has settled into a war of attrition along a front running from Kharkiv through Donetsk and Zaporizhzhia to Kherson. Ground change is small: DeepState data cited by RussiaMatters showed a net Russian gain of only about 47 km2 in the four weeks to Oct 26, while Kyiv claims it retook more than it lost in October and that Russia lost a record 49,000-plus troops killed or wounded that month (Ukrainian General Staff figures, not independently verified). The air war is intensifying, with record Russian missile-and-drone salvos repeatedly cutting power in Kyiv and other regions, while Ukraine hits Russian refineries and sends hundreds of drones toward Moscow. On Nov 2 Russian heavy bombs killed at least 31 people at an aid site in Komyshuvakha, Zaporizhzhia, according to Ukrainian officials cited by AP. A local truce for occupied Oleshky took effect Oct 27, and US-mediated working-level talks are scheduled in Abu Dhabi for Nov 10-11, but Russia still demands all of Donbas and Kyiv refuses.

US envoy Witkoff announced US-mediated Ukraine-Russia working-level talks in Abu Dhabi on Nov 10-11, preceded by allied meetings in Brussels on security guarantees.
Ukrenergo said Kyiv and four regions were still without power after repeated overnight Russian strikes on energy facilities.

us_impact.text: Washington is the lead mediator, with envoys Witkoff and Kushner expected at the Abu Dhabi talks, and US-made air defenses and SpaceX's Starlink remain central to Ukraine's defense. Ukraine's strikes on Russian refineries and a new Trump-approved deal letting Russia ship diesel to North America tie the war directly to US fuel markets. Failed talks would likely bring fresh requests for US weapons and funding, against a nuclear-armed adversary.

conflicts.watch: Whether the Nov 10-11 Abu Dhabi talks produce any de-escalation, or whether Russia launches the further mass strike on energy and logistics that Kyiv's intelligence warned of.
conflicts.outlook: Expect heavy strikes on energy on both sides through the Nov 10-11 Abu Dhabi talks; a real ceasefire looks unlikely while Russia demands all of Donbas.
conflicts.consensus: Ukrainian, independent Russian, Gulf and US outlets agree on the strikes and the talks; casualty and territory figures come from the warring sides and differ.

conflicts.name: Black Sea shipping attacks
conflicts.status: NATO adds patrol aircraft and radars after a dozen-plus ships hit; Contship Jet sank
conflicts.summary: Russia has long tried to choke Ukraine's sea exports, and since early October 2026 drone strikes widely blamed on Moscow have hit at least a dozen merchant ships near Romanian and Bulgarian waters. Romanian and Bulgarian officials count roughly 30 sailors killed or missing; recent sinkings include the Khoryv off Constanta on Oct 23 and the Contship Jet off Shabla on Oct 28. Romanian F-16s shot down two jet-powered Geran drones near Sulina on Oct 17, and after a special North Atlantic Council session NATO pledged more patrol aircraft, radar and drones for the Black Sea. Russia has not claimed every attack, but its defence ministry says some targeted ships carried military or dual-use cargo for Ukraine. War-risk insurance costs for the Black Sea have soared.

latest.text: CNN reported more than a dozen ships struck in the past month, some near or inside the territorial waters of Romania and Bulgaria, and said the Contship Jet later sank.
After seven strikes on cargo ships near Romania and Bulgaria last month, NATO said it would deploy maritime patrol aircraft, radars and drones to the Black Sea.
Three sea drones struck and disabled the container ship Contship Jet about 21 nautical miles off Shabla, Bulgaria; all 18 crew were rescued.
A drone sank the cargo ship Khoryv about 13 nautical miles off Constanta, killing one sailor and leaving three missing; Romania blamed Russia.
NATO said it will send additional patrol aircraft and drones to the Black Sea after drone attacks on merchant ships.
Romanian F-16s shot down two jet-powered Russian Geran drones over Romanian waters near Sulina, and NATO called a special Black Sea session.

us_impact.text: Romania and Bulgaria are NATO treaty allies whose waters and airspace are being hit, so a lethal strike on allied territory could trigger alliance consultations that bind the US; NATO has already sent extra patrol aircraft and drones. Secretary of State Rubio said in September that Ukraine had hit US-linked vessels, showing US commercial interests are exposed on both sides. Soaring war-risk premiums and disrupted grain and fuel cargoes push up global shipping and commodity costs.

conflicts.watch: A strike inside Romanian or Bulgarian territorial waters causing NATO casualties, or a request to invoke Article 4, would escalate this.
conflicts.outlook: Reporting points to more drone strikes on shipping and a growing NATO air and sea presence off Romania and Bulgaria. It hinges on whether Russia keeps targeting ships near NATO waters and how allies respond.
conflicts.consensus: CNN (US) and South African outlets agree that attacks have accelerated near Romania and Bulgaria and that NATO is reinforcing. Romania blamed Russia for the Oct 23 strike; accounts of casualty counts per ship differ, and I could not reconcile them.

conflicts.name: Russia–NATO tension: Poland, Baltics, Kaliningrad
conflicts.status: Tusk says Poland foiled border 'provocation' near Kaliningrad; GROM units deployed
conflicts.summary: Russia has pressured NATO's eastern flank for years with sabotage, airspace violations and nuclear signaling around its heavily militarized Kaliningrad exclave between Poland and Lithuania. On Sept 30 Reuters reported that Moscow sent NATO an informal note threatening to use all its forces, including nuclear weapons, if the alliance tried to cut Kaliningrad off; NATO condemned the threat. In September a Russian military helicopter from Kaliningrad crossed briefly into Polish airspace, and on Oct 18 a drone, apparently Ukrainian and likely diverted by Russian jamming, exploded on a car in Lithuania, with Vilnius and Warsaw disputing its route. On Nov 2 Poland launched a week-long security operation with counterterrorism police and GROM special forces along the Kaliningrad border after Polish and allied intelligence warned of possible sabotage or armed incursions; PM Tusk said suspicious movements were seen near the border.

latest.text: Tusk said Poland prevented an attempted provocation on the Kaliningrad border overnight, giving few details, and said extra police and counter-terrorism units were sent after warnings of sabotage or an armed incursion in early November.
Tusk described the incident as people with flashlights moving along the border and warned that escalation from Russia may continue for some time.
Russia's state news agency TASS reported the GROM deployment as aimed at preventing sabotage that Polish and foreign intelligence allege is planned.
Tusk said intelligence warned for weeks of possible provocations, including armed men entering Poland, as GROM and police units deployed along the Kaliningrad border until at least Nov 8.
Polish police reinforced Podlasie and Warmia-Masuria after military intelligence and allied services warned of imminent sabotage near Kaliningrad.
Lithuania said a drone that hit a car on its soil was of Ukrainian origin and entered from Poland, which Warsaw disputed.

us_impact.text: Poland and Lithuania are NATO treaty allies, so an armed incursion or attack from Kaliningrad could invoke Article 5 and US military commitments; Tusk has said he discussed the sabotage threat with NATO's top commander, US Gen. Alexus Grynkewich. Moscow's explicit nuclear threat over Kaliningrad and the Suwalki corridor makes this the most likely flashpoint for a direct US-Russia confrontation in Europe.

conflicts.watch: An armed incursion, a confirmed sabotage attack, or a Russian military response on the Kaliningrad border would push this to red.
conflicts.outlook: Poland expects the pressure to continue through at least the first half of November, with units on the border until at least Nov 8. It hinges on whether any of the sabotage or incursion warnings turn into a confirmed incident.
conflicts.consensus: France 24, AP and the Moscow Times report Tusk's account alike: odd night-time movement was spotted and Poland mobilised forces. Tusk himself could not be fully certain it was a provocation, and Russian state media (TASS) call the sabotage claims alleged and unproven.

conflicts.name: Moldova drone spillover / Transnistria
conflicts.status: Record Russian drone incursions; a Geran fell near homes and Moldova expelled a diplomat
conflicts.summary: Moldova, a non-NATO country bordering Ukraine and home to the Russian-backed breakaway region of Transnistria, is absorbing growing spillover from Russia's drone war on Ukraine. Its defence ministry counted 19 airspace violations in October and 67 in the first ten months of 2026, out of 104 since 2022, with six drones exploding on the ground in October, including five near Causeni on Oct 3. In late October a Russian Geran crashed less than 100 meters from homes in Telenesti district on a course toward Transnistria's Camenca district, and Chisinau expelled a Russian embassy staffer. No casualties have been reported, and Moldova says it needs stronger air defenses.
